items.title: Rust 1.100
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/11/12/Rust-1.100.0/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50472038 Points: 204 # Comments: 115
items.content:
The Rust team is happy to announce a new version of Rust, 1.100.0. Rust is a programming language empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software.

If you have a previous version of Rust installed via rustup , you can get 1.100.0 with:

If you don't have it already, you can get rustup from the appropriate page on our website, and check out the detailed release notes for 1.100.0 .

If you'd like to help us out by testing future releases, you might consider updating locally to use the beta channel ( rustup default beta ) or the nightly channel ( rustup default nightly ). Please report any bugs you might come across!

After 10 years and 5 failed stabilization attempts, the never type is finally stable ! This also completes the project goal for this work.

The never type, spelled ! in code, is the canonical uninhabited type. It represents the type of diverging computations – computations which never resolve to any value – where any code that follows is unreachable. Expressions that terminate control flow, such as return , break , and std::process::exit , also have the type ! .

Since having a value of the never type is impossible, Rust permits a never-to-any coercion, allowing to turn ! into any other type (this is what distinguishes it from any other uninhabited types). This can be used, for example, to not return a value from one of the branches of a match or an if :

While the never type could already be used and observed this way, and even named in the return type of functions ( -> ! ), this release allows naming the never type anywhere:

Additionally this release changes Infallible to be an alias to the never type. That makes all old APIs that used Infallible be compatible with using ! . This was the plan ever since the introduction of Infallible and is one of the reasons why the never type stabilization was so hard (waffle gave a talk about some of the troubles of the stabilization).

Unfortunately, to allow changing Infallible , we had to introduce a breaking change. This release changes the "never type fallback" from () to ! in editions before 2024 (i.e. 2015, 2018, and 2021), similarly to what has already been done in edition 2024 . This should largely be unnoticeable, but can affect code in some rare cases (for example when ignoring a result of a function returning a generic parameter). Note that this change might also make the compiler detect more code as unreachable.

We tried to minimize the impact of this breaking change as much as possible, by providing future compatibility warnings far in advance and releasing fixes to public crates that have been broken by this. If a dependency is failing due to issues with the never type, consider updating it, as a fix might have already been released for it.

This release brings about the stabilization of the core parts of allocator_api , enabling library authors to define custom allocators that can be used together with certain standard library types - currently Vec and Box . These are enabled through the newly-stabilized Allocator trait.

This is the foundation of the Allocators 1.0 project goal . A lot remains to be done still, including expanding the API surface usable with custom allocators and stabilizing their use on more collections and pointer types; with the core trait and design out of the way though, expect to see more being stabilized soon!

The Drop trait in Rust makes it possible to run code when a variable goes out of scope, regardless of whether we return , ? , or panic. Drop being a part of types means that in Rust you never have to close a socket .

Implementing Drop can however feel a little inconvenient when all you want is to run some code unconditionally when a function exits. This is why we’re introducing core::mem::DropGuard : a new helper type that runs a closure when dropped.

DropGuard takes two arguments: a variable and a closure. It implements Deref and DerefMut so you can keep working with the variable as normal. But when dropped it runs the closure and consumes the variable.

DropGuard also implements a dismiss method which returns the variable from the guard without running the destructor. This makes it possible to quickly implement all-or-nothing transaction-like APIs with a rollback. Here is an example implementing a parser which uses a guard to roll back mutations in case of failure:

As Rust's unsafe code guidelines are still being decided, it became clear that it would be very useful to decide what exactly it means to create zero-sized types in an unsafe way, and what we should recommend for people to do this.

This question is answered in Rust 1.100 with a single function: std::mem::conjure_zst .

Instead of transmuting () , MaybeUninit::uninit().assume_init() , or various other incantations, this is the dedicated way to create a value of a zero-sized type when you know that doing so is safe to do. If an inhabited type has no size, we know exactly what value it must be: nothing.

Of course, APIs often rely on the inability to construct such types for safety, and that's why this function is unsafe. For example, PyO3's Python<'py> is a zero-sized marker token that represents holding the Python GIL (global interpreter lock). Many of Python's APIs require holding this lock to be safe, but conjuring a token from thin air would allow safe PyO3 calls to violate that precondition.

Cargo now reports unused dependencies to users, e.g.

A limitation of this warning is that it will only appear when building every build target that may use an entry in a dependencies table. For example, running cargo check --bin foo won't show warnings for unused [dependencies] because another bin may be present that uses them. No warning will be shown for unused dev-dependencies because there isn't a way to ensure every development build target is built.

items.title: Google DeepMind Staff Tap the UK Government to Escalate Their Unionization Fight
items.summary: After initial talks stalled, workers at Google DeepMind are trying to bypass company management in their bid to unionize.
items.content:
Google DeepMind employees in the UK have asked the government to intervene in a push to unionize the artificial intelligence lab.

On Thursday, the Communication Workers Union and Unite the Union—put forward by Google DeepMind staff as joint representatives—filed an application with the Central Arbitration Committee, a government body that resolves disputes between employers and unions.

The application, which was seen by WIRED, asks the CAC to confirm that the unions have enough support from workers to trigger a unionization ballot. The company would be required by law to respect the results. If successful, roughly 1,000 staff working in product-focused roles at Google DeepMind would qualify for union membership.

The escalation follows a series of meetings between employees, the unions, and company representatives over voluntary unionization, which left staff with the impression that their demands weren’t being taken seriously.

“They’ve been ignored. They feel like their problems have been minimized,” John Chadfield, national officer for technology at the CWU, tells WIRED. “Management has refused to come to the table. They sent it to the HR and labor relations people, who dealt with it as an administrative box-ticking exercise.”

“We respect the right of employees to make an informed decision about whether or not to join a union,” Google DeepMind spokesperson Tom Hewett tells WIRED in a statement. “We have consistently listened to both those seeking to unionize and those opposed, and have acted in good faith from the outset. We remain committed to constructively participating in this process, and have maintained open and transparent communication with our employees and the unions throughout.”

The push to unionize began in February 2025, when Alphabet, Google’s parent company, removed a pledge from its ethics guidelines stating that it wouldn’t use AI for purposes like weapons development.

“When I joined, we really made a big deal about the principles—the red lines. We were really looking to benefit humanity and make the world a better place,” a Google DeepMind employee, who asked to remain anonymous for fear of backlash, tells WIRED. “A lot of this is about reestablishing that ethical and moral framework that we started with.”

The employees pushing for unionization object in particular to agreements between the company and the US and Israeli militaries. If they succeed in unionizing, they intend to demand that Google backs out of those contracts.

“We feel extremely concerned about the direction that this technology is going in,” says a second Google DeepMind employee, who asked to remain anonymous for the same reason as the first employee.

The company has previously defended its deals with government organizations.

“We are proud to be part of a broad consortium of leading AI labs and technology and cloud companies providing AI services and infrastructure in support of national security,” Jenn Crider, a Google spokeswoman, told The New York Times in April. “We remain committed to the private and public sector consensus that AI should not be used for domestic mass surveillance or autonomous weaponry without appropriate human oversight.”

In an email delivered to all UK staff on Thursday, seen by WIRED, the Google DeepMind employees involved in the unionization push appealed to their colleagues to participate in the ballot, which they expect to take place in the coming months. “We want a union, we want collective bargaining, and we want a say in how AI is developed and deployed,” they wrote.

The group also hopes it can establish a playbook that employees at other major AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic can follow in the UK.

“It’s pretty rare that there’s been an industry that exercises such dominance and power over the economy, where there’s so little opportunity for employees or regulators to have any checks and balances,” the second Google DeepMind employee says. “We want to show what can happen when employees collectively organize and articulate a shared vision for the way their technology should be used.”

Hydrogen brings cutting-edge intelligence to everyone.

SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google

Your browser does not support the audio element.

Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.

Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.

To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity . Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 , Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster. For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.

Beyond multi-model workflows, Hydrogen is a major standalone upgrade for teams migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash. It delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence — finishing tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting while more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%), cutting fabricated claims by more than 5x, and adapting cleanly when a tool call fails or a search returns empty. It also matches or outperforms competing models in its class across core developer and enterprise workflows:

Using Hydrogen for on-the-fly 3D coding, Geminisland lets anyone add to a shared voxel island from a single prompt to generate custom structures live on the map that players can walk around and explore in first person. Try the live app .

Paired with our new Gemini front end design skill in Google Antigravity, Hydrogen built an e-commerce storefront in one shot complete with a WebGL2 topographic shader, pinned four-stage scrollytelling, a thermal split-slider, a 3D wireframe spec card, and a live finish configurator. Try the live app and the Gemini front end design skill .

In Google Antigravity, Hydrogen turned Google Sheets into an animated pixel canvas by shrinking thousands of cells combining Python, native =LET(...) formulas, and conditional formatting to paint and animate full-motion scenes directly inside a live spreadsheet.

Starting from a YouTube keynote video and a design template in Google Antigravity, Hydrogen generated a multi-slide presentation directly in Google Slides, then ran an autonomous audit-and-fix loop to catch overlapping text and clean up every slide layout.

With Gemini in Google Sheets, Hydrogen can help teams rapidly turn financial data into interactive models that dynamically adjust based on various forecasting scenarios, generating outputs over 30% faster than previous models in Sheets canvas.

We built Gemini 4 Hydrogen for real-world usability. Hydrogen’s four thinking levels — low, medium, high (default), and a new xhigh tier — offer a wide range of options across quality, latency, and cost, scaling in a smooth, predictable progression so you only wait and pay for the reasoning depth a task requires. Across thinking levels, Hydrogen matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class while often finishing tasks faster and using fewer output tokens.

For consumers, Gemini 4 Hydrogen makes it easier to get things done, staying on track and following instructions more closely across multi-turn conversations.

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen makes your everyday assistant even more helpful — it’s better at following your guidance, calling the right tools, and getting you to a reliable output with less back-and-forth.

items.title: Jensen Huang Basically Lit More Than $1 Trillion on Fire in Less Than a Month
items.summary: Since the scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy began, Nvidia has lost an eye-watering sum from its market value.
items.content:
On Thursday morning, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned from the company that had become, in many ways, synonymous with its chief executive.

Less than an hour later, when the markets opened, Nvidia’s stock had lost roughly $546 billion in market value. Though it has rebounded somewhat, the last weeks of scandal—including a reported second affair with an Nvidia employee—have tanked the chipmaker’s valuation by more than $1 trillion.

Huang’s very public downfall began in late October, when The New York Times reported that the CEO had a “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based chip buyer Megaspeed and an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. (The two are not known to be related.) At that time, Nvidia’s market cap was around $5.2 trillion.

On November 8, Nvidia announced it was investigating its CEO, after Jensen publicly acknowledged the affair. By the following morning, roughly $1 trillion had been erased since the scandal started.

If you hang out with a certain type of person who thinks of themselves as a daytrader, they might have talked about “buying the dip” over drinks last weekend. If you believe Nvidia can thrive without Huang, there’s still time! The dip has dipped even further. But the early consensus seems to be that this could be more of a prolonged plunge.

“Huang is irreplaceable,” Ryan Fedasiuk, a senior fellow at the think tank Foundation for American Innovation, told WIRED last week. “He built Nvidia into the juggernaut it is today, and he was the visionary behind the GPU, which has sustained the intelligence revolution.”

There are very real questions about what the end of Huang means for the global economy. Not only are Nvidia’s chips used to train most major AI models, but the company has also invested billions in a number of other tech companies. As of an August regulatory filing , Nvidia owned nearly $30 billion worth of Intel stock and roughly $21 billion of SpaceX stock.

For now, Nvidia’s loss is other chipmakers’ gain. AMD shares are up 28 percent over the past five days, and Broadcom is up nearly 16 percent. Nothing to see here.

items.summary: I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang's second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn't he be? He's placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he's the only CEO Nvidia has e
items.content:
A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here.

I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang’s second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn’t he be? He’s placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he’s the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L’état c’est moi.

Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out.

Why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained?

Fascinating. First of all, when I asked on Monday “Who else is Jensen Huang fucking?” I did not expect to get answers this fast — somebody, potentially somebody on the board (as we’ve seen in other incidents ), wanted the story out there. Second, why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? This is not an industry that cares about that kind of thing — just ask Eric Schmidt and Bill Gates. My guess is that the second affair is a pretext for action, and this all goes back to the original story from last week: that Huang was honeypotted by an alleged Chinese spy. Whatever was going on with neocloud Megaspeed might be much, much worse than we know, and what we know is pretty bad : business listings that led to “a Malaysian data center and shopping mall, a near-empty office in Singapore and a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur.”

Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46.

Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China . But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.”

Megaspeed was Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, but Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore office a month ago to find “no signs of activity.” Another building tenant told the reporters, “It is always dark for as long as it has been here. I hardly see anyone visiting or in the office.” The sole director of Megaspeed, Tan Yong Pong, appears to have vanished . The Singaporean company that owns Megaspeed, Swiftdata, has listed an office that belongs to an interior design firm as its business address.

Megaspeed is only part of the story

Incidentally, Alice Huang has surfaced in Beijing . The Financial Times says she’s barred from Singapore for giving police “inaccurate information.” Oh, and reportedly her companies invested in Chinese AI company DeepSeek and promised them Nvidia’s Blackwell chips? Fun!

Megaspeed is only part of the story, I think. There are two Chinese chip-related scandals that could cause serious problems for Nvidia, and both feature people with close ties to Huang. One is Megaspeed, which involves Huang’s maybe-spy affair partner. The other centers on Super Micro (which, horribly, does business as Supermicro), a partner of Nvidia run by one of Huang’s old friends, Charles Liang. Super Micro’s cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, along with Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, allegedly defrauded the US by serving as a passthrough for a front company to buy $2.5 billion of Nvidia chips for Alibaba. The front company, not named in the indictment, is Thailand-based OBON , according to Bloomberg . Liang and Super Micro have not been charged.

But these incidents may not be the end of Nvidia’s problems. Take for instance, more recently, New Matrix — another company that barely exists , and yet is an approved buyer of Nvidia chips. It is, in fact, one of several approved companies that “have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China,” according to The New York Times.

The question, of course, is how high this all goes

Huang has insisted that Nvidia has seen “no evidence of any AI chip diversion.” He’s been pretty emphatic on that point , actually. I am now wondering if that is even a little bit true. If the board is cutting Huang loose, there’s probably more on chip smuggling allegations coming.

More substantively, Nvidia reportedly intervened in a 2025 Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed , which was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips — halting the investigation. Since the scandal broke, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appears to have become the fall guy for this, with Axios reporting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent “confronted” him about failing to note Megaspeed as a national security concern and Politico saying “ more than half a dozen Republicans have demanded answers” from him .

The question, of course, is how high this all goes. After all, Huang was awfully buddy-buddy with President Donald Trump, who was informed about Huang’s maybe-spy girlfriend in 2025 and apparently did nothing about it. Incidentally, Nvidia has reportedly donated $25 million to Trump’s planned ballroom . This is what gangster tech regulation looks like.

I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know?

items.title: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open source AI after Jensen Huang’s exit
items.summary: Hugging Face's CEO pledged to keep fighting for open source AI after Huang's exit, raising questions about Nvidia's $12.9 billion acquisition.
items.content:
Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue briefly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday, calling it a “really sad day.” Nvidia had announced its plan to acquire the platform for open source AI models in September for $12.9 billion, making it the second-largest acquisition in the company’s history, just behind that of chipmaker Groq’s assets for $20 billion in December 2025.

“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!,” Delangue wrote on X.

This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!

The post is interesting as it implies that Huang’s departure is potentially worrying to open source advocates, and he’s attempting to offer reassurance.

As Nvidia’s CEO, Huang was known as a strong advocate for open source AI and open-weight models, which is why there could be concerns about how a company that’s no longer under his leadership will now approach this space.

After Nvidia announced its plans to acquire Hugging Face, the U.S. Department of Justice began making inquiries about how the deal would impact competition in the AI market, Reuters reported in October . While Nvidia pledged that the platform would preserve open support, it would also allow the company to control a major distribution channel for AI models.

The Hugging Face deal is still scheduled to close in the first half of 2027. Requests for further comment on the deal status and whether Hugging Face has spoken yet with Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress were not returned.

Huang’s advocacy for open source and open-weight AI has long extended beyond Hugging Face. In July, the CEO published an AI policy letter as his first-ever post on the social network X . The letter, which was signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, IBM, Palantir, and others, urged the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models. It said models that “anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure” are an important part of the AI ecosystem because they make AI “more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.”

Huang also wrote that open-weight models expand access to the AI economy, strengthen competition, and give customers greater control, as they know they won’t become locked into a single provider. “Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” his post on X stated.

For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter. AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty.… pic.twitter.com/t02bi51N4C

In August, Nvidia also announced a $6 billion deal with the coding startup Poolside to help build out an open AI ecosystem in the U.S. to help the country compete against Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Kimi K3, The Wall Street Journal reported at the time. Last month, Nvidia expanded its Nemotron family of open-weight models with a large 120-billion-parameter model for agents used by the enterprise as well as with two new lightweight Bolt models that run on PCs.

Earlier this year, Huang promoted open source AI during his January keynote address at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, noting that open source models have “really revolutionized artificial intelligence.”

items.title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks
items.summary: The airline said it will not allow customers to use AI agents to book flights and manage reservations.
items.content:
United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations.

The airline is the latest American corporate giant to prevent customers from using AI agents and autonomous assistants to access their systems. The move comes as airlines and banks are struggling to differentiate between real customers and AI systems operating on their behalf, such as when users share their logins with their AI assistants. Sharing passwords with apps and assistants can create security risks if those credentials get leaked or exposed.

United warns that “sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles.”

The airline also warns of a risk of violating federal aviation rules, such as requiring that a human completes flight check-ins to acknowledge that their bags do not contain banned substances.

“As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants,” the airline said in a statement . “This work includes updates to our booking, ticketing and distribution policies.”

The airline’s move follows a warning from banks, including Bank of America, which last week urged customers not to share their passwords with their AI assistants.

items.title: Show HN: My $300 embroidery machine needed a subscription, so I built my own app
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/simpsoka/zigzag Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50470488 Points: 213 # Comments: 85
items.content:
ZigZag is a visual embroidery editor built in Rust for performance, with built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) support so AI agents can create and edit designs alongside you. Turn SVG artwork into stitches, fine-tune it in the editor, and export PES, DST, EXP, JEF, or VP3 for broad compatibility with embroidery machines—or send designs directly to a Brother Skitch (PP1) over Bluetooth .

Draw in Illustrator, draw in ZigZag, or let an agent draw. The Rust engine and zigzag command-line tool power the same workflow outside the editor.

Stitching on a Brother Skitch (PP1)

Download the video (MP4, 1080p) · Original post on X .

For Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, macOS 11 or later. Open the DMG, then drag ZigZag into Applications. The release is signed and notarized by Apple. No Rust installation is needed.

Download ZigZag for Windows — the ZigZag-<version>-x86_64-windows.zip asset on the latest release.

For 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1709 or later) and Windows 11. Unzip it and double-click ZigZag.exe . Windows SmartScreen warns on apps without a Microsoft-trusted signature the first time they run; click More info → Run anyway . No Rust installation is needed.

Release notes and checksums · Publishing a release

Linux needs the usual X11/Wayland and OpenGL dev libraries for gui . libdbus is vendored for ble .

Satins wider than 7 mm are auto-split (shorter, staggered stitches) and use auto spacing (narrow columns more open, wide ones denser).

On a Mac with Rust and the Xcode command line tools ( xcode-select --install ):

--release signs with your Developer ID and has Apple notarize the app and the DMG, so it opens on any Mac without warnings. Once, beforehand: add a Developer ID Application certificate (Xcode › Settings › Accounts › Manage Certificates › +), make an app-specific password at account.apple.com, and save the notarization credentials in your keychain:

The app bundles the studio, the zigzag command-line tool and the MCP bridge. To use the command line from anywhere: ln -s /Applications/ZigZag.app/Contents/MacOS/zigzag /usr/local/bin/zigzag . For Claude Desktop, point the MCP config at /Applications/ZigZag.app/Contents/MacOS/zigzag-mcp .

Without --release the app is signed ad hoc, not notarized. It opens normally on the Mac that built it. On another Mac, macOS blocks it the first time: open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway (on macOS 14 and earlier, right-click the app and choose Open instead). macOS asks for Bluetooth permission the first time you send to the Skitch.

The approved embroidered icons live in packaging/macos/AppIcon.png (light) and packaging/macos/AppIcon-dark.png (dark). The Mac build regenerates both multi-resolution .icns files; run bash packaging/macos/make-icons.sh to regenerate them separately. Finder and the unopened app use the light icon. While the studio is running, its Dock icon follows the app's light/dark theme, including the ZIGZAG_THEME=light|dark override.

Laid out like Illustrator, styled like a Mac app:

Tools down the left edge: Select (V), Direct Selection (A), Hand (H), Pen (P): click for corners, drag for curves (Option breaks the handles, Shift keeps 45°, Space moves the point being placed); while drawing, Option lends it the Anchor Point tool (drag a segment to bend it, a handle to move it alone, click a smooth point for a corner) and ⌘ lends Direct Selection (drag a point or handle, then keep drawing), and on a selected path Option-drag bends a segment too. Illustrator's Pen group is behind it: Add Anchor Point (+) clicks a point onto an outline without changing its shape, Delete Anchor Point (-) clicks one out (Option swaps the two while held), and Anchor Point (Shift+C) converts points between smooth and corner and drags one handle alone. Press and hold the Pen (or right-click it) for the group's flyout, Option-click it to step through the group, or tear the group off into a toolbar of its own with the strip at the flyout's edge; the Shape tools work the same way. Brush (B), with VectorCraft's path clean-up tools in its group: Smooth (drag along a path to take the wobble out: fewer points, smoother curves; Smoothness in the bar above), Path Eraser (drag across a path to cut that part away) and Join (scrub between two open ends to join them, or an open path's two ends to close it). Shapes (M rectangle, L ellipse, \ line; hold or right-click for polygon and star), Fill Angle (G), Measure (I), Text (T). Below them, the selection's thread swatch: click it for the thread color picker.

Curves, the Illustrator way: the Pen clicks corners and click-drags curves (Option while dragging breaks the handle for a sharp turn; Shift keeps points and handles at 45°; hold Space to move the point you're placing). Click the last point to make it a corner, or drag from it to start the next curve in a new direction. Click the first point to close a shape; Enter, Esc, ⌘-click or another tool ends a line and keeps it. With a path selected, the Pen continues it from an open end, adds a point on its outline, deletes a point you click, and Option-click turns a point corner ↔ smooth (Option-drag pulls out new handles). While drawing, click another open path's end to join the two into one. The cursor shows what a click will do. Direct Selection drags points and handles of any shape from your SVG (circles and rects become paths); dragging a curve bends it under the pointer (Option-drag bends a straight one; a plain drag moves it); Delete removes points, arrows nudge them.

Smart guides while drawing (View › Smart Guides, ⌘U): Pen points, shape corners and dragged points land on other objects' anchors and centers, where two outlines cross, on an outline, on 45° rays from the last point (level and upright handles too), or in line with any of those, with a magenta label saying which ("anchor", "intersect", "path", "align"…). With Shift, a point keeps its 45° angle and slides into line with the nearest target.

items.title: SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions
items.summary: SoftBank lost over $3 billion preordering natural gas turbines to power AI data centers. Here's what the loss means to power markets.
items.content:
SoftBank might not be the first to invest in a hot trend, but when it does, it goes big.

Witness its $30 billion bet on OpenAI in early 2025 or its announcement in February that its SB Energy subsidiary would spend $33 billion on a 9.2-gigawatt natural gas power plant. If you can’t be first, be biggest, I guess.

That philosophy apparently spilled over into procurement, where orders were also supersized. Starting about two years ago, SoftBank reportedly put down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed.

The decision to over-order undoubtedly helped secure turbines and speed up SoftBank’s projects.

“SB Energy did not have a choice except to overbook turbines in the future if they wanted some turbines right away,” Peter Gardett, CEO of Noreva , told TechCrunch via email.

The energy world was caught off guard by the swiftness and magnitude of AI’s rising power demands. Queues for turbine orders now extend into the early 2030s . As natural gas was shaping up to be a go-to power source for the AI boom, CEO Masayoshi Son bet that by deploying his investment firm’s significant war chest, he could corner a portion of the market. If the AI world wanted power for its data centers, it would have to come to him.

Now that bet appears to have fizzled. SoftBank announced a $7.1 billion quarterly loss on Tuesday, with over half of that stemming from losses related to power-generating equipment. The investor had paid turbine manufacturers nonrefundable deposits to secure orders, and now it considered much of those worthless.

The move was also a costly bit of price discovery, Gardett said. Rather than overpay and potentially still be short of turbines, SoftBank overpaid and over-ordered.

“This charge is just that price discovery finally happening,” Gardett said.

The magnitude of that misplaced bet — over $3 billion — reflects some of the electricity mania that has overtaken the AI world. Faced with years-long waits to connect to the grid, many hyperscalers and developers have turned to natural gas as a sort of energy security blanket, something that is proven and familiar.

As AI data centers spend more time in operation, their operators are getting a better feel for what’s required to keep them operating. Natural gas might seem like a safe bet, but there are still risks, including winter curtailments when supplies dip and demand spikes, Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy at Ascend Analytics , told the Equity podcast Wednesday.

In light of that, Nelson said the grid might still be their best bet. Most data centers would be best served by a grid connection, albeit a smaller one than they might normally request. To make up for the shortfall, large batteries are a cost-effective choice, Nelson said. They’d help shave peak loads or ride out requests from the utility to curtail electricity use.

Data center operators might be coming to that same conclusion, leading the natural gas market to develop more slowly than SoftBank expected.

SoftBank’s natural gas-related losses are unlikely to have a domino effect, leading to mass cancellations of gas power plants. AI’s power demand appears to be too large for that. For now, natural gas is riding high, though SoftBank may have found its ceiling.

items.title: ‘The end of Tesla!’: Cybertruck diehards turn on Elon Musk after he pulls the plug
items.summary: The Cybertruck is heading to that shiny cyber-dumpster in the sky, leaving the folks who built online identities around Elon Musk's polarizing pickup feeling bereft. Usually, Musk's fanbase treads lightly around their idol's mercurial decisions. This time, however, the truck's de
items.content:
Tesla’s polarizing pickup is heading to the scrap heap, leaving its biggest online boosters feeling betrayed and questioning Musk’s next big pivot.

The Cybertruck is heading to that shiny cyber-dumpster in the sky , leaving the folks who built online identities around Elon Musk’s polarizing pickup feeling bereft. Usually, Musk’s fanbase treads lightly around their idol’s mercurial decisions. This time, however, the truck’s demise has sparked rare backlash within the Tesla community — aimed squarely at the guy who signed its death warrant.

Troy Meekhof, who posts on numerous social platforms under the moniker “The Cybertruck Guy,” has been vocal about his disappointment in Musk’s decision to wind down Cybertruck production by the end of summer 2027. (The original plan was to start winding down production in the spring, but then Musk decided to extend it a few months.)

In a 33-minute video on YouTube, Meekhof argues that Tesla never fully committed to making the Cybertruck a success, citing a lack of advertising, confusing pricing changes, and the decision to shift focus before the truck could fully establish itself in the market.

“It feels like they didn’t try to make Cybertruck a success,” he said.

He also had choice words for Musk’s reasons for ending the Cybertruck’s short run to make room at Giga Texas for the fully autonomous Cybercab: “Cancelling all of your best products... in favor of an autonomous platform that remains both software and regulatory constrained... seems like an absolutely terrible idea,” Meekhof vented.

The Cybertruck wasn’t the only Tesla product to meet an untimely end — at least according to those with stakes (and often stock options) in the company’s success. Earlier this year, Tesla discontinued the Model S and Model X , two of its flagship vehicles. With the end of the Cybertruck, Tesla is now left with just the Model 3 and Model Y as vehicles you can actually buy. (The Semi is strictly a commercial vehicle, while the Cybercab’s availability as a consumer product remains dubious, at best.)

“Cancelling Cybertruck after all the years of getting it to production to ‘make room for CyberCab’ is a lame excuse,” @TeslaXplored wrote on X. “There are like 500 CyberCabs in one city that only Tesla influencers are riding in. Taking away consumer cars instead of building what the people want will be the end of Tesla!”

He added, “Very sad what happened to Tesla over the last 5 years.”

Meanwhile, at least one prominent aftermarket company is offering to step in and pick up the mantle. Unplugged Performance, which makes aftermarket accessories, said it would produce the Cybertruck and other vehicles on the truck platform under license, with investors funding the effort: “Worth a conversation?”

Musk, for his part, seems less interested in litigating the particulars of Cybertruck production and more intent on selling a vision of Tesla’s future centered around the Cybercab and humanoid robots. “Cybercab will do a majority of all passenger miles in any jurisdiction where it is not prohibited by law,” Musk wrote on X earlier this week. “Obvious to anyone with eyes and a brain.”

He also pushed back on claims that the Cybertruck was killed because it was unprofitable. “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate,” Musk said . “We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

To be sure, Cybertruck sales have been disappointing over its entire production run. Musk initially theorized that Tesla could sell 250,000-500,000 Cybertrucks annually, but the actual numbers have been f ar below those projections . Last year, Tesla is estimated to have sold around 20,000 trucks; the company is on track to sell fewer than that this year.

Whether Musk’s autonomous utopia pans out or ends up joining the Cybertruck in the vaporware graveyard remains to be seen. For now, the stainless-steel wedge that was supposed to be the ultimate symbol of an indestructible future has become a monument to Musk’s shifting attention span — and a stark reminder to Tesla’s most loyal boosters that in Elon’s world, nothing should be taken for granted.

items.title: Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots
items.summary: Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to turn everyday moments into better photos.
items.content:
A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives users access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.

Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to get access to better photos.

The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.

The duo saw a gap in the editing tools on the market and believed that although editing tools can be powerful for enhancing photos, they aren’t very effective at fixing a photo that wasn’t captured well in the first place. Phota Labs changes that by focusing on fixing the shot itself while preserving the natural appearances of those in the image.

“Phota is your personal photo assistant that can make great photos for any moment you want to keep before you even ask, which means that it’s a very proactive experience,” Zhang told TechCrunch in an interview. “Think of it almost like a photographer or virtual photographer who looks over your camera roll and tries to understand what’s happening and how they could have taken that photo for you on the spot for that scene.”

The idea is to use AI to transform photos, whether that’s turning a wide-angle group photo into a tighter portrait or transforming a selfie into a regular shot.

Users can choose from different photography styles that determine how AI transforms their images, ranging from subtle edits that preserve the original lens and composition to more dramatic transformations that introduce effects like fish-eye lenses, alternative angles, and entirely different perspectives.

While some people turn to ChatGPT and other generative AI tools to enhance or edit images, these tools can often alter a person’s appearance, especially when working with blurry photos because they don’t know what that person actually looks like.

“For Phota, we built our own tech,” Zhang said. ”We built this personalization technology that actually learns about people’s identity and is able to preserve them in any transformation we do to a photo.”

Images edited with Phota Labs feature invisible watermarks that identify them as altered by AI when shared on social platforms.

The startup is initially targeting people who take tons of photos and like to share them on social media, but don’t want to deal with the tedious process of editing photos. Over time, the founders envision a broader audience, from retirees looking to create beautiful photos for their grandchildren to parents who want to share polished family albums with friends and relatives.

“We have this obsession with authenticity,” Xia said. “I think there’s so much value in connecting AI with real moments and making sure those photos are not perfect, in a sense. That’s why we spend a lot of research into understanding personal context, into building this identity model because we want to make sure the photos are authentic. They’re just better photos of the same moment, rather than saying, ‘Oh, this is an AI image’.”

Xia said beta users were excited to see better versions of moments they had actually lived and saw the results as photos of real memories rather than AI-generated images. The founders discovered that users were taking more photos because they knew Phota Labs could enhance them later.

“We’re turning something that’s unusable into something that people want to print,” Zhang said. “People who just love photos but never really got into editing can now experience professional quality that could never have been possible. So, I think that meant so much to us. There’s so many cherished moments for photos, and we really want them to be actually meaningful and something that you can remember.”

In terms of funding, the company raised a $5.6 million seed round led by a16z last year.

Phota Labs is launching as a free app to build an initial user base before exploring a freemium model. The startup also plans to launch an Android app in the future.

items.title: Nintendo Takes Down Emulators and Firmware in Massive GitHub DMCA Sweep
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.ign.com/articles/nintendo-takes-down-switch-emulators-and-mod-chip-firmware-in-massive-github-dmca-sweep Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50469994 Points: 236 # Comments: 164
items.content:
Nintendo has sent four DMCA takedown notices to GitHub targeting two Nintendo Switch emulators, Yuzu and Citron Neo, along with mod chip firmware.

This isn't the first time Nintendo has sent takedown notices to GitHub, and it's not even the first time it's tried to take down Yuzu , but the focus this time around seems to be on firmware for mod chips. This particular firmware had 144 repositories, all of which have been removed by GitHub and replaced by a DMCA takedown notice. Mod chips like Picofly can be soldered onto the Nintendo Switch's mainboard, and can be flashed with this firmware to circumvent Nintendo's copy protection.

GitHub has posted Nintendo's November 6 DMCA notice , which says, "The Nintendo Switch console and video games contain technological protection measures ('TPMs') that permit the Nintendo Switch console to interact only with legitimate Nintendo video game files. This process protects Nintendo’s copyright-protected video games, (...) by preventing users from playing pirated copies of Nintendo’s video games on the Nintendo Switch console and by preventing users from unlawfully copying and playing Nintendo’s video games on unauthorized devices."

However, while this takedown has effectively wiped out a ton of repositories with mod chip firmware, it seems like it's still being hosted elsewhere on the site, according to TorrentFreak . It's possible, though, that Nintendo isn't finished yet; back in 2024, Nintendo effectively took down 8,500 copies of Yuzu by issuing a takedown that targeted 12 different mirrors of the emulator.

This particular takedown also comes a few days after emulators were able to run the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on PC, so this could be a sign that Nintendo is winding up its lawyers to crack down on emulation once again.

If anything, emulation is a completely different beast in 2026 than it was even in 2024, thanks to the rise of AI. There's already been a wave of AI-made mashup mods that took over Twitter for a couple of weeks, and led Anthropic to coding in a lock to prevent Claude from outright copying games . Game developers have started cracking down on AI ports of games, too. Just last month Rockstar had to take down a browser version of GTA 5 , and Bethesda took down an AI-generated Fallout New York game .

글로벌뉴스 입력 :2026/11/13 01:10

시전 MCP를 통해 첫 기능 제공, 시전 포트폴리오 전반으로 빠르게 확대할 계획

시카고 , 2026년 11월 13일 /PRNewswire/ -- 소비자 및 미디어 인텔리전스와 커뮤니케이션 기술 분야의 글로벌 선도 기업 시전(Cision)이 11월 12일, 시전 포트폴리오 전반의 폭넓고 깊이 있는 데이터, 전문성, 역량을 전문 AI와 결합한 시전 인텔리전스(Cision Intelligence)를 선보였다고 밝혔다. 시전 인텔리전스는 브랜드가 변화를 더 일찍 포착하고 확신을 갖고 행동하도록 돕기 위해 설계됐으며, 이러한 강점을 하나의 에이전틱 대화형 경험으로 연결하는 것을 목표로 한다. 첫 기능은 브랜드워치 컨슈머 리서치(Brandwatch Consumer Research)를 시작으로 시전 MCP(Cision MCP)를 통해 제공된다.

Cision Intelligence brings together AI with specialist data, expertise, and capabilities into one agentic experience to help marketing, PR, and comms teams understand what’s happening, what it means for their business, and what to do next.

시전 인텔리전스는 한 번 개발해 시전의 전체 솔루션 제품군과 지원되는 외부 도구 및 에이전트로 확장하는 공유 AI 토대 위에 구축됐다. 한 번의 구축으로 모든 곳에서 사용하는 구조이기에 개선 사항이 이를 구동하는 모든 제품과 지원 도구에 적용될 수 있어, 고객은 어디에서 일하든 같은 인텔리전스를 얻는다. 기능이 확장되면 팀은 이미 사용하는 도구에서 질문을 조사하고, 중요한 사항을 파악하며, 인사이트를 행동으로 옮길 수 있게 된다.

시전의 가이 아브라모(Guy Abramo) 최고경영자 는 "고객들은 시장이 어떻게 변하고 있는지, 그것이 자사 비즈니스에 어떤 의미를 지니는지, 그리고 다음에 무엇을 해야 하는지 알고 싶어 한다"고 말했다. 이어 "시전 인텔리전스는 우리의 전문성을 대화형 경험에 담아 고객이 이러한 질문에 답하도록 돕는다. 우리의 목표는 고객이 의사결정을 내리는 모든 곳에서 시전의 폭넓은 인텔리전스를 활용할 수 있게 해, 행동에 나설 수 있는 더 큰 명확성과 확신을 제공하는 것"이라고 덧붙였다.

초기 접근은 AI 도구와 에이전트가 신뢰할 수 있는 데이터 및 서비스와 연동되도록 하는 개방형 표준인 모델 컨텍스트 프로토콜(Model Context Protocol)을 기반으로 구축한 시전의 연결 서비스 시전 MCP를 통해 제공된다. 첫 출시 버전은 고객을 브랜드워치 컨슈머 리서치 에이전트에 연결해 지원되는 도구와 워크플로에 소비자 인텔리전스를 도입한다. 시전은 제품 에이전트를 추가하고 시간이 지나면서 더 폭넓은 연결 워크플로를 개발하는 방식으로, 다른 솔루션 전반으로 접근을 빠르게 확대할 계획이다.

신호를 연결해 사람들이 놓치는 것을 발견하기

오디언스는 의견을 형성하고 결정을 내리는 과정에서 검색, 소셜 미디어, 뉴스 보도, AI가 생성한 답변 사이를 오간다. 이러한 신호가 서로 어떻게 연관되는지 이해하면, 고립된 상태에서는 파악하기 어려운 기회와 우려를 발견할 수 있다.

제품 출시가 긍정적인 보도와 활발한 소셜 미디어 반응을 낳는 동안 신뢰성과 경쟁사 대안에 관한 검색은 늘어날 수 있다. 이러한 신호를 함께 이해하면 브랜드가 관심과 구매 사이에 놓인 질문을 파악하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.

시전 인텔리전스의 계획된 확장은 트라잔(Trajaan)의 검색 인텔리전스, 브랜드워치의 소비자 리서치와 소셜 미디어 관리, 시전원(CisionOne)의 미디어 인텔리전스와 PR 워크플로, PR 뉴스와이어(PR Newswire)의 배포 및 Multichannel Amplification™ 등 포트폴리오의 폭넓은 역량을 활용한다. 이처럼 연결된 접근 방식은 고객이 변화를 이해하는 단계에서 어떻게 대응할지 결정하는 단계로 나아가도록 돕는다.

시전의 짐 댁스너(Jim Daxner) 최고 제품 책임자 는 "이제 모든 팀이 AI를 이용할 수 있다. 차이는 AI가 무엇을 토대로 하느냐에 있다. 범용 어시스턴트는 대체로 비슷한 공개 정보를 바탕으로 작동한다"고 말했다. 이어 "시전 인텔리전스는 기업이 어디에 투자할지를 좌우하는 질문에 우리의 전문 데이터와 전문성을 가져온다. 우리는 팀이 이미 쓰는 AI 도구에서 소비자 인텔리전스부터 시작해 시전 전반으로 확장해 나간다"라고 덧붙였다.

일상적 의사결정에 더 가까워진 소비자 인텔리전스

첫 출시 버전은 시전 MCP를 통해 네 가지 기능을 제공한다:

이러한 기능은 함께 팀이 소비자가 하는 말을 탐색하고, 새롭게 나타나는 대화의 배경이 된 질문을 조사하며, 주목할 만한 변화를 파악하도록 돕는다. 고객은 브랜드워치 컨슈머 리서치와 함께 이 추가 접근 경로를 이용할 수 있다.

시전의 제프 멀린스(Jeff Mullins) 최고 기술 책임자 는 "고객은 자신이 선택한 환경에서 우리의 전문 인텔리전스를 활용할 수 있어야 한다"고 말했다. 이어 "당사의 공유 AI 토대 덕분에 제품과 경험 전반에서 발전된 기능을 재사용할 수 있다. 시전 MCP는 오늘날 그 전문성에 접근하는 또 다른 길을 열어 주며, 브랜드워치 컨슈머 리서치부터 시작해 더 연결된 워크플로를 구축해 나간다"고 덧붙였다.

cision.com/cision-intelligence/ 에서 시전 인텔리전스와, 이것이 비즈니스에 어떤 의미를 가지는지 확인할 수 있다.

기존 제품도 계속 제공되므로, 고객은 현재 사용하는 솔루션에서 계속 작업할 수 있다.

시전 소개 시전은 소비자 및 미디어 인텔리전스, 참여, 커뮤니케이션 솔루션 분야의 글로벌 선도 기업이다. 시전은 PR 및 기업 커뮤니케이션, 마케팅, 소셜 미디어 전문가가 오늘날 데이터 중심 세계에서 앞서가는 데 필요한 도구를 갖추도록 돕는다. 깊은 전문성, 독점 데이터 파트너십, 시전원 , 브랜드워치 , 트라잔 , PR 뉴스와이어 를 비롯한 수상 경력의 제품으로 시전은 포춘 500(Fortune 500) 기업의 84%를 포함한 7만 5000개 이상의 기업과 조직이 가장 중요한 오디언스를 선보이고, 보이며, 이해하고 이해받을 수 있도록 지원한다.

items.title: I'm making LLMs work on small and old devices
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/hyperionaidev/smolmaxxing/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50468888 Points: 233 # Comments: 85
items.content:
Run the biggest language model you can on the smallest hardware you own.

TV boxes, old tablets, single-board computers and routers all have a CPU, some RAM and flash storage that sit idle most of the day. smolmaxxing finds the biggest model each of them can really run, then pushes it further with custom kernels, careful memory use and weights streamed from flash. Every number in this repo was measured on the device itself.

Both devices run 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models on about 1 GB of RAM by keeping only part of each model in memory and reading the rest from flash as it's needed.

More devices (phones, single-board computers, routers) are coming. The techniques aren't tied to one box: the 1-bit kernel needs only basic NEON, and the flash streaming works on any Linux or Android device with more model than RAM.

All of it is a patch on llama.cpp . The main ideas:

docs/how-it-works.md has every technique with its measured gain.

The quickest start is a ready-made model file from Hugging Face. They need the patched llama.cpp: stock llama.cpp can't load them.

MIT . The llama.cpp patches are derivatives of llama.cpp (MIT). Model weights keep their own licenses, and the evaluation texts are Wikipedia excerpts (CC BY-SA 4.0).

Built on llama.cpp and llama2.c . Models from Qwen , unsloth (GGUFs and importance matrices), PrismML (Bonsai), inclusionAI (Ling-mini-2.0), tablinum (Moon-Beam), bartowski and mradermacher (GGUFs), Google (Gemma) and stories260K . The iPad is jailbroken with Amethyst . The banner uses Archivo (SIL OFL) and is rendered by tools/banner/render.sh . The 🤏 logo is the pinching-hand emoji from Google's Noto Emoji (Apache 2.0).
